power.title: Power prices in Norway
power.lead: Hourly spot prices for all five Norwegian price areas. Pick an area, compare it with the national average, and see which hours of the day are worth waiting for. Everything is fetched in the browser from an open API.
power.tomorrowLocked: Tomorrow's prices are published no earlier than 13:00
power.chartCaption: Bar chart of the hourly spot price in {zone} ({city}) for {date}, with the national average as a dashed line.
power.chartNote: Colours mark the cheapest, middle and priciest third within this particular day — not fixed price thresholds. A cheap hour in July and a cheap hour in January have little to do with each other.
power.compareLead: Daily average in all five price areas, cheapest first. Select an area to see it in the chart.
power.compareNote: The national figure is a plain mean of the five price areas, not weighted by consumption or population.
power.notPublishedTitle: Tomorrow's prices are not out yet
power.notPublishedBody: Tomorrow's prices are set in the European market and published no earlier than 13:00. Try again later today.
power.errorGeneric: Failed to fetch power prices. It could be the network, or the source could be down right now.
power.sourceNote: prices exclude VAT at the source, are fetched from ENTSO-E in euros and converted using the daily rate from Norges Bank. Government support is not deducted.
power.mapAria: Map of Norway divided into the five price areas, coloured by daily average. Select an area to view it.
power.mapNote: Simplified map. The outline is drawn by hand and the borders are straight lines — the real price area borders follow the power grid, not county lines.

contrast.title: Contrast checker
contrast.lead: Paste two colours and get the WCAG contrast ratio, along with which grades it actually clears. The tool also audits this page's own colours while you are standing on it.
contrast.formats: Accepts #a63c1f, a63c1f, rgb(166 60 31) and "166 60 31" — the last one is the format this site stores its colours in.
contrast.suggestion: The nearest colour clearing 4.5:1 is {hex}, which is {direction}. It gives {ratio}:1.
contrast.previewBody: Body text at a normal size. This is where the 4.5:1 requirement applies, and where most failures hide — small grey labels that looked perfectly fine on the screen of whoever made them.
contrast.auditLead: The figures below are read from the custom properties of the page you are on right now, not from a copy. Switch to dark mode and they change immediately.
contrast.auditNote: Green clears 4.5:1 and is fine for body text. Amber clears 3:1 and is fine for large headings, borders and icons. Red clears neither.
contrast.storyBody: When this site's colour system grew four category hues, I measured every combination rather than trusting my eye. That turned up --c-faint sitting at 2.86:1 against the card surface — below the 3:1 floor. The colour was darkened, and the tool you just used is that same calculation wrapped in an interface. Then the tool found a second fault: 3.44:1 does clear 3:1, but --c-faint is used for real 11px text — labels, captions, axis values — and text that size requires 4.5:1. The colour had to be darkened again. The first measurement found the bug; the tool found what I had misunderstood about it.

about.title: About me
about.lead: I am {age}, based in Trondheim, and working through a BSc in computer engineering at NTNU.
about.siteNote: This site is built from scratch with Vue 3, TypeScript and Tailwind — no template, no page builder. The source is on GitHub if you want to see how it fits together.
about.closing: Most of what I know isn't in a CV. It's in the projects.

p1.title: Make it work first
p1.body: I build the simplest version that actually runs end to end, then improve from there. It is easier to refine something that works than to guess the right architecture up front.

p2.title: Write for whoever reads it next
p2.body: Code gets read far more often than it gets written. I spend time on naming, structure and writing down why something is done a certain way — usually 'whoever reads it next' turns out to be me, six months later.

p3.title: Ask early
p3.body: I will happily spend an hour trying to work it out myself, but if I am still stuck after that, I ask. Being stuck for two days in silence helps nobody.

contactPage.title: Get in touch
contactPage.lead: Questions about something I've built, an idea you want to talk through, or just saying hello? Email is the fastest way.
contactPage.responseNote: I usually reply within a day or two.

projectsPage.lead: Things I built to learn something specific. Each one has its own page covering what went well, what was hard, and what I would do differently.
projectsPage.moreOnGithub: Everything else — including the half-finished things — lives on GitHub.
